episode.episode_title: The OpenCode Breach: When Convenience Becomes a Liability
episode.episode_description: Anomaly Innovations reports a security breach affecting OpenCode Console users. We look at the risks of storing API keys in developer tools and what this means for your workflows.
episode.selection_reason: The lead verified story from today's Sapiver Forge Daily Brief.

selected_story.headline: OpenCode breach exposes user API keys
selected_story.source_title: Anomaly Innovations, behind coding agent OpenCode, says a breach hit ~1.4% of OpenCode Console users and their API keys, in a "large scale distillation attack" (Walter Schulze/Startup Fortune)

short.title: OpenCode breach exposes user API keys
short.description:
This incident serves as a stark reminder that storing third-party API keys in developer tools creates a single point of failure, potentially allowing attackers to hijack expensive or sensitive AI agent workflows.

Read today's Sapiver Forge Daily Brief: https://suite.sapiverpress.co.uk/daily-brief/
short.script: OpenCode breach exposes user API keys. Anomaly Innovations reported a security breach affecting 1.4% of OpenCode Console users, resulting in the exposure of stored OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys. Read the Sapiver Forge Daily Brief.
